To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) wage bargaining institutions affect the adaptability of the economy to structural change; and (2) this is true even after controlling for the effects of the other variables in our analysis.

(1) centralized wage bargaining institutions are conducive to labor market flexibility and (2) wage bargaining centralization is conducive to economic performance, particularly in the case of the labor market.

(1) centralized wage bargaining institutions are associated with a more flexible labor market, as measured by the rate of structural unemployment and the rate of structural change; (2) this positive effect of centralized bargaining institutions on labor market flexibility is not due to a negative effect of centralized bargaining on the rate of structural employment; (3) centralized bargaining institutions are also associated with lower unemployment rates; (4) this effect is not due to the effect of bargaining institutions on the rate of labor market flexibility.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, "What is the relationship between wage-setting institutions and the adaptability of the economy?"
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relationship between wage-bargaining institutions and economic performance is complex.
the Swedish experience is not a clear-cut case in favor of the corporatist view.
the Swedish model is not the best way to go.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Swedish model of wage bargaining, which is based on centralized negotiations between the peak organizations of employers and unions, is not a good model for the United States and other countries.
the Swedish model has not only survived the crisis, but has also been strengthened and has become more flexible and adaptive.
the Swedish system of wage bargaining has been a major factor in explaining the country's good economic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the relationship between centralized bargaining institutions and economic outcomes depends on the adaptability of the wage setting institutions.
wage bargaining institutions can play a significant role in shaping structural change.
